screenings.description: Tech founder Elizabeth Holmes invites Nathan Fielder to film her before she’s sent to prison.

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: An aging pickpocket (John Turturro) has to race against time to avoid a vengeful crime family.

screenings.title: Club Kid
screenings.description: A hard-partying NYC club promoter discovers he has a 10-year-old son that he never knew about.

screenings.title: Gunvor Nelson Program 2
screenings.description: “These three films, among Nelson’s most beautifully crafted works, were made during return trips to her home country, leading up to her move back to Sweden in 1993 after teaching for more than two decades at the San Francisco Art Institute. Frame Line blends still photographs (some of which she paints on) and moving images, showing the full range of her artistry as she revisits her past. Red Shift, filmed at her parents’ home in Kristinehamn, is a unique hybrid film with scripted and documentary elements, with Nelson, her daughter Oona, and her mother as ‘performers,’ punctuated by readings of letters from Calamity Jane to her daughter. Old Digs weaves together a murmuring soundtrack of a family gathering with roaming color images of a rustic village, layered with cut-out images added through stop-motion animation.” —Series curator David Schwartz

screenings.title: Fjord
screenings.description: From two⁠-⁠time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close⁠-⁠knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice. In Norwegian, English, Romanian and Swedish with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Wild Horse Nine
screenings.description: Two CIA agents wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies on Easter Island.

screenings.title: You Can See Everything
screenings.description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss.

screenings.title: Paper Tiger
screenings.description: James Gray’s latest drama follows two brothers whose bond is threatened by a dangerous scheme.

screenings.title: Rate It X
screenings.description: First released in 1985, RATE IT X stunned audiences and critics alike with its unflinching look at how sexism and sexual exploitation are embedded in American media and culture. Directors Lucy Winer and Paula de Koenigsberg traveled across the United States interviewing men who profited from—and helped perpetuate—stereotyped and sexualized images of women. Advertising executives describe how sex is used to sell product. Hustler magazine’s creator of the notorious “Chester the Molester” cartoon proudly displays drawings depicting a predatory adult man entrapping young girls. A fundamentalist minister tells us that Adam shirked his responsibility by allowing Eve to lead. The flamboyant producer of a popular cable show roams the streets of New York City in a silver lamé jumpsuit, video camera in hand, asking young women, “Would you like to flex into a hallway and pose nude?”

screenings.title: Mouse
screenings.description: It’s 2002, and best friends Minnie and Callie are heading into their senior year of high school, with Minnie long living in the protective shadow of the charismatic and admired Callie. When their friendship is suddenly upended at the start of the summer, Minnie struggles to define her own identity and forms a complicated relationship with Callie’s poised, attentive mother, pulling her further from her own chaotic home.

screenings.title: Dinner With Friends + Q&A
screenings.description: After the parties, jobs, and hook-ups throughout their twenties and into their thirties, eight friends are trying to hold on to their group as they get older and life gets complicated. Over a series of dinners, the group deals with loyalty, loss, and an uncertain future as relationships shift and secrets are unraveled, with each dinner bringing its own dynamic shifting announcement of reconciliation, unexpected relationships, and betrayal. The city is crumbling, the climate is changing, and worries about the future of the world are making it hard for this group of friends to stay together. But they’ll come to realize everything would be much harder if they don’t.

screenings.title: A Fox Under a Pink Moon
screenings.description: Dir. Mehrdad Oskouei & Soraya. 2025, 96 mins. Iran, Turkey, Greece. DCP. In Farsi with English subtitles. A moving, artful, and surprising collaboration between the legendary Iranian filmmaker Mehrdad Oskouei and a whip-smart teenage artist, A Fox Under a Pink Moon follows Afghani refugee Soraya’s relentless efforts to escape an abusive marriage in Tehran and join her mother in Austria. But rather than the cliché frame of master and muse, Oskouei remotely directed Soraya to tell her own story, from both her reality and her imagination. In addition to many attempts to cross the border into Europe, Soraya escapes and resists oppression through her dark and unfettered artwork, which often features an enigmatic fox and weeping clown. It is her work that gives the film its shape and aching intimacy, from the watercolor animations derived from her drawings, to her smartphone video diaries tracking five years of survival separated from her home and loving family. Poetic and raw, A Fox Under a Pink Moon is as electric and courageous as its heroine, making it easy to see why this film won awards all over the world and is in serious discussion for the 2027 Oscars Awards. screenings.title: Fist Church
screenings.description: Every other Sunday we’ll be mining the depths of VHS, VCD, DVD, and the darkest corners of the internet to bring you the wildest post-brunch experience you’re likely to have. So, get faded on Bloody Mary’s (leave the PCP at home) and come kick your feet up while we play fast and loose with the rules and witness people fight hopping vampires, ninjas, swordsmen and more. The movies won’t be announced, but trust us – on this one we wouldn’t steer you wrong.

screenings.title: Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall
screenings.description: Experience Geese frontman Cameron Winter’s 2025 concert, filmed by Paul Thomas Anderson.

screenings.title: Fatherland
screenings.description: The writer Thomas Mann and his daughter embark on a road trip across a divided Germany.

screenings.title: Gunvor Nelson Program 3
screenings.description: "“Gunvor Nelson’s experience as a painter before becoming a filmmaker is at its most evident in these strikingly graphic films, all of which involve hands-on manipulation of the surfaces and textures of still and moving images. Light Years and Light Years Expanding use collage techniques while traversing the Swedish landscape, by train in the former and car in the latter. The final two works are made entirely in the studio. Nelson describes Natural Features as ‘a free associative and playfully bizarre form of animation. Here I used mirrors, water, toys, cut-outs, photographs, paint, ink … in many different combinations. The central theme is face.’ Experimenting with video, Nelson performs magic in Trace Elements, creating a visual dance between her camera and her shadow.” —Series curator David Schwartz

screenings.title: That Day, On The Beach
screenings.description: The little-screened debut feature by Yang, prophet of and proselytizer for the Taiwanese New Wave, features Sylvia Chang and Terry Hu as two female friends, an unhappily married housewife and a concert pianist, brought together after a 13-year separation: their process of catching up illustrated through an innovative, ingeniously layered flashback structure which shows the director’s air for formal experimentation already fully in operation. Shot by renegade cinematographer Christopher Doyle, also on his first feature, Yang’s gorgeous and deeply felt memory piece/mystery uses its intricate structure to explore, among other things, “the ways in which patriarchal authority stunts young people’s lives.” US theatrical premiere of new 2K restoration.

screenings.title: Steps
screenings.description: In this charmingly offbeat action comedy, Cinderella’s “evil” stepsister Lilith steals the Fairy Godmother’s wand and shatters the story as we know it.

screenings.title: You Can See Everything
screenings.description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss.

screenings.title: Gigi
screenings.description: Dir. Vincente Minnelli. 1958, 115 mins. U.S. 35mm. With Leslie Caron, Louis Jourdan, Maurice Chevalier, Hermione Gingold. The CinemaScope frame is crammed with exquisite detail in this thrillingly visualized musical adapted from a story by Collette about a girl’s coming-of-age in wealthy turn-of-the-century Paris. Minnelli’s film is both tender and sly, a social satire of sexual mores as well as a moving tale of an innocent’s entrance into a complicated world in which women’s options are limited. The winner of nine Oscars (a record at the time), including Best Picture, Director, Cinematography, Art Direction, Costume Design, Song, and Score (by My Fair Lady composers Lerner and Loewe), Gigi is a triumph on every level, like a Toulouse-Lautrec painting sprung to giddy life. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / $7 MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

screenings.title: Fatherland
screenings.description: ★★★★★ “Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master.” – Phil de Semlyen, Time Out “A perfectly cut jewel of a movie... The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... Told with exacting restraint yet as layered as the lacquer on an ebony Biedermeier console, this forms a loose triptych with Pawlikowski’s last two features, IDA and COLD WAR, both of which were set at least partly behind the Iron Curtain... It is immaculately performed by Zischler and especially Hüller, grounding the film throughout with an uncanny, expressive stillness. But it is also exquisitely rendered in the same boxy ratio and silvery monochrome lensing Pawlikowski and DP Lukasz Zal (THE ZONE OF INTEREST) deployed on IDA and COLD WAR, and scrupulously detailed down to the ruined buildings, sharply cut suits, surly restaurant service and eclectic selection of jazz, classical and folk tunes chosen by Pawlikowski, all of which is sure to set discriminating viewers swooning.” – Leslie Felperin, The Hollywood Reporter

screenings.title: Threeasfour: Full Circle
screenings.description: Avant-garde designers and best friends Gabi Asfour, Angela Donhauser, and Adi Gil have spent 25 years working together as the NYC fashion collective threeASFOUR. Although they have built an impressive reputation and a following that includes Björk, Marisa Tomei, and Chloë Sevigny, they find themselves struggling to pay the rent on their Chinatown studio while financing the intricate creations for their next runway collection. Drawing from a captivating trove of archival footage alongside intimate observations of the trio at work, Sean Ono Lennon forges an affectionate portrait of uncompromising artists who have chosen experimentation over commercial success and a moving reflection on artistic collaboration and creative resilience. Presented with support from The Endowed Fund for Emerging Filmmakers and The Roy Lichtenstein Foundation Fund 2026 95 MIN. USA IN ENGLISH, GERMAN, AND ARABIC WITH ENGLISH SUBTITLES ASSEMBLY RELEASING

screenings.title: Screen Tests + Screen Tests Revisited, Pgm 2
Profit Motive and the Whispering Wind
screenings.description: Boston-based filmmaker and former Harvard Film Archive curator John Gianvito had made a few films before the 20th century became the 21st, but he would wind up emerging as one of the definitive filmmakers of the current century during its first decade. His six years of work on Gulf War I cri de cœur The Mad Songs of Fernanda Hussein wound up serving as one of the definitive commentaries on the upcoming century when it premiered in 2001. Mad Songs served as a work of inadvertent commentary on the bloodlust spurred by the Twin Tower attacks, and the Gulf War II that was going to come about as a result. It was also a work of intensely personal cinephilia-inspired curation: Griffith- and Wyler-adjacent structuring of multiple war-at-home storylines was melded with archival footage and performance documentary, resulting in a bold and sprawling hybrid work. Despite fierce advocacy from notable champions in Chantal Akerman, Peter Watkins, Jonathan Rosenbaum, and Dennis Lim, it was not an easy film to see in 2001 and it has not gotten much easier since. He’d take another six years to make his next film, this time decidedly aimed at the domestic. Profit Motive and the Whispering Wind (2007) was a film whose more minimalist scale and running time didn’t reduce its power. Its simultaneously rousing and despairing analysis, courtesy of Howard Zinn, marked a turn towards a more domestic issue: how America eats its rabble rousers but leaves a tribute to them later. The groundwork laid by the champions of Mad Songs resulted in Profit Motive finding more of an audience, and it subsequently being named the Best Experimental Film of 2007 by the National Society of Film Critics.

screenings.title: The Oldest Profession
screenings.description: A meld of ATG and radical pink sensibilities, Noboru Tanaka’s guerrilla-shot apostasy captures its subjects writhing in both agony and pleasure over the course of a sordid Osaka summer.

screenings.title: Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall
screenings.description: Experience Geese frontman Cameron Winter’s 2025 concert, filmed by Paul Thomas Anderson.

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: An aging pickpocket (John Turturro) has to race against time to avoid a vengeful crime family.

screenings.title: Emperor of the North
screenings.description: Inspired by the writings of legendary hobo Leon Ray Livingston, under the pen name “A-No.1,” Aldrich’s tale of the risks run rail-riding in the ’30s northwest stars Lee Marvin as top tramp A-No.1, locked in a battle royale struggle with Ernest Borgnine’s fascistic, hobo-hatin’ conductor Shack on the speeding #19 of the Oregon, Pacific and Eastern Railroad, while Keith Carradine’s rascally fellow stowaway looks on. Featuring gorgeous location photography, suicidal stuntwork on speeding period locomotives, and bone-breaking action, Emperor of the North is Aldrich at his brutal best.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Raise the Red Lantern
screenings.description: China/Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Zhang Yimou Starring Gong Li, Saifei He, Jingwu Ma, Cuifen Cao In Mandarin with English subtitles Approx. 125 min. Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films and The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.title: Rate It X
screenings.description: First released in 1985, RATE IT X stunned audiences and critics alike with its unflinching look at how sexism and sexual exploitation are embedded in American media and culture. Directors Lucy Winer and Paula de Koenigsberg traveled across the United States interviewing men who profited from—and helped perpetuate—stereotyped and sexualized images of women. Advertising executives describe how sex is used to sell product. Hustler magazine’s creator of the notorious “Chester the Molester” cartoon proudly displays drawings depicting a predatory adult man entrapping young girls. A fundamentalist minister tells us that Adam shirked his responsibility by allowing Eve to lead. The flamboyant producer of a popular cable show roams the streets of New York City in a silver lamé jumpsuit, video camera in hand, asking young women, “Would you like to flex into a hallway and pose nude?”

Memento
screenings.description: The indie sensation that put a young English director named Christopher Nolan on the map for good, this strikingly original, ornately structured neo-noir stars Guy Pearce as Leonard, a man on a mission of revenge after a savage attack that left his wife dead and him with anterograde amnesia, unable to store new short-term memory and forced to rely on an elaborate note-taking system in order to continue his single-minded pursuit of justice. “A brilliant feat of rug-pulling… [Nolan is] clearly excited by the way the medium can manipulate time and information, folding straightforward events and simple motives into Möbius strips of paradox and indeterminacy… Like an existential crossword puzzle, or a pungent 50’s B-thriller with a script by Jorge Luis Borges.” —The New York Times

screenings.description: Four years before her Palme d’Or triumph with Anatomy of a Fall, Triet produced this comic thriller starring Virginie Efira in the title role as a psychotherapist who, fed up with her métier, decides to return to writing fiction—and, in the person of one of her patients, a young, tumultuous actress named Margot (Adèle Exarchopoulos), finds an absolutely irresistible source of literary inspiration. Impassioned performances by both leads make Sibyl a compelling study in obsession and self-delusion, with the added inducement of Anatomy star Sandra Hüller’s appearance in a side-splitting role as the director of a film-within-the-film.

screenings.title: Orfeo
screenings.description: In the classic Greek tragedy, a snake bites Eurydice on her wedding day, and her new husband, Orpheus, travels to the Underworld to bring her back. Virgilio Villoresi’s expressionistic adaptation of the tale is based on Dino Buzzati’s 1969 Poema a fumetti, Italy ‘s first graphic novel. The film is a modern reimagining with an aesthetic untethered from reality: a kaleidoscopic journey through time and place, reflecting on art, love, mystery, eroticism, melancholy, life, and death.

screenings.title: Rome, Open City
screenings.description: “A STILL-THRILLING CALL TO CONSCIENCE AND HOPE! Shot with electrifying urgency months after Rome’s liberation… a cinematic landmark [that brought] Italian neorealism to world-wide attention. Born of wartime trauma and a desire for unity in the new Italy that would come, ROME, OPEN CITY has lost little of its power.” – Kristin M. Jones, Wall Street Journal Read the full review. “THE MOST PRECIOUS MOMENT OF FILM HISTORY!” – Martin Scorsese “ROSSELLINI’S NEOREALIST MASTERPIECE... Aldo Fabrizi is compelling as a sympathetic priest, as is Marcello Pagliero as a cool Communist. But towering over all is Anna Magnani, as a pregnant widow, mother and bride-to-be... Plain-spoken, tender and yet indomitable, she provides the film’s central anima.” – Andy Webster, New York Times “Rossellini’s tense, bloody, death-haunted film conjures an authenticity that’s based less on its quasi-documentary style than on a vision that brings ideas to life. It offers a template for a postwar renewal of Italy, as well as Italian cinema.” – Richard Brody, New Yorker “A LEGENDARY CINEMATIC ACHIEVEMENT! Its justly celebrated documentary aesthetic and naturalistic performances, aided by the filmmakers’ budgetary restrictions and the ruinous state of the postwar Italian film industry, help the work achieve moments of devastating, near miraculous beauty.” – Oleg Ivanov, Slant Read the full review. “The fame of Rossellini’s brutal, melodramatic account of the underground resistance to the Nazi occupation rest on its extraordinary immediacy and its rough, documentary look; at its most startling, it seems ‘caught’ rather than staged. Many Americans, used to slick war films, reacted to it as if it actually were caught… The movie gave us a cross-section of a city under terrible stress.” – Pauline Kael “Rossellini’s Neo-Realism masterpiece... It scarcely matters how many times you watch it... For some of us, this film might evoke the wonder of a great-grandchild listening in on grown-up reminiscences. Nodding at the substance. Smiling at the style.” – Lisa Kennedy, Variety “[A] rich doc crafted from gorgeously restored footage. screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Rate It X
screenings.description: First released in 1985, RATE IT X stunned audiences and critics alike with its unflinching look at how sexism and sexual exploitation are embedded in American media and culture. Directors Lucy Winer and Paula de Koenigsberg traveled across the United States interviewing men who profited from—and helped perpetuate—stereotyped and sexualized images of women. Advertising executives describe how sex is used to sell product. Hustler magazine’s creator of the notorious “Chester the Molester” cartoon proudly displays drawings depicting a predatory adult man entrapping young girls. A fundamentalist minister tells us that Adam shirked his responsibility by allowing Eve to lead. The flamboyant producer of a popular cable show roams the streets of New York City in a silver lamé jumpsuit, video camera in hand, asking young women, “Would you like to flex into a hallway and pose nude?”

Paisan
screenings.description: PAISÀ Italy, 1946 Directed by Roberto Rossellini Starring Carmela Sazio, Robert Van Loon, Dots Johnson Approx. 126 min. 35mm. The story of Italy’s liberation, told in six episodes, traveling from the first Allied landing in Sicily to the battle of the Po Delta, PAISAN demonstrated that OPEN CITY had been no fluke. Conceived on a vaster scale, with a considerably higher budget, and international distribution from MGM, PAISAN is a national epic that still startles for its immediacy, its technical mastery, its unpredictable rhythms. Scenes of unbearable suspense on the streets of Florence alternate with lighter fare, such as the doctrinal scuffles between Italian monks and American chaplains in Romagna. Stitched together like a newsreel (and skillfully edited to blend in stock footage and suggest off-screen pyrotechnics with creative sound effects), PAISAN became a worldwide sensation, an intellectual action film that pictured recent history with an unprecedented heft and scope. The film became a lodestar for filmmakers from Gillo Pontecorvo to Martin Scorsese, with the latter remarking, “The result... is still startling: it’s like seeing reality itself unfolding before your eyes.” 35mm print courtesy Cinecittà.

screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. screenings.description: Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

screenings.title: That Day, On The Beach
screenings.description: The little-screened debut feature by Yang, prophet of and proselytizer for the Taiwanese New Wave, features Sylvia Chang and Terry Hu as two female friends, an unhappily married housewife and a concert pianist, brought together after a 13-year separation: their process of catching up illustrated through an innovative, ingeniously layered flashback structure which shows the director’s air for formal experimentation already fully in operation. Shot by renegade cinematographer Christopher Doyle, also on his first feature, Yang’s gorgeous and deeply felt memory piece/mystery uses its intricate structure to explore, among other things, “the ways in which patriarchal authority stunts young people’s lives.” US theatrical premiere of new 2K restoration.

screenings.title: The Host
screenings.description: When a terrifying creature rises from the Han River and brings chaos to Seoul, single dad Gang-du (Song Kang-ho, Parasite) will stop at nothing to rescue his daughter from the clutches of the horrifying Host. Equal parts creature-feature thrill ride and poignant human story, Oscar-winning visionary Bong Joon Ho’s first global smash remains an incredible action drama and propulsively entertaining modern classic.

screenings.title: Sad Vacation
screenings.description: The third and final film of Aoyama’s “Kitakyushu Saga,” adapted from his own novel, stars Tadanobu Asano as Kenji, a young man still nursing the wounds of an unhappy childhood as he goes through the desultory motions of various odd jobs, who catches sight of an opportunity for closure—or, perhaps, revenge—when one night he recognizes the wife of one of his employers as the mother who’d abandoned him years ago, and conspires to infiltrate their household. A rich, moving human drama of families arbitrarily assigned and chosen, its large ensemble cast handled adroitly, and the proceedings given a striking, somber beauty by prodigiously gifted cinematographer Masaki Tamura.

screenings.title: Tangles
screenings.description: Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Sarah Silverman, Abbi Jacobson, Seth Rogen and Bryan Cranston voice a family struggling with their mother’s Alzheimer’s diagnosis in this deeply moving, animated adaptation of Sarah Leavitt’s acclaimed graphic novel.

screenings.title: All of a Sudden
screenings.description: Japan’s Official Selection for Best International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards® WINNER, BEST ACTRESS (VIRGINIE EFIRA & TAO OKAMOTO), 2026 CANNES FILM FESTIVAL In the latest film by Oscar®-winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi (DRIVE MY CAR), Virginie Efira (BENEDETTA) stars as Marie-Lou, the progressive director of a nursing home in the Parisian suburbs. Her life changes when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), Japanese playwright. As the two women reckon with the lives they have lived, they find new ways to make sense of the time that remains. Following caregivers as they navigate the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a film that rests fully in the present, attentive to the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and human connection. screenings.description: Avant-garde designers and best friends Gabi Asfour, Angela Donhauser, and Adi Gil have spent 25 years working together as the NYC fashion collective threeASFOUR. Although they have built an impressive reputation and a following that includes Björk, Marisa Tomei, and Chloë Sevigny, they find themselves struggling to pay the rent on their Chinatown studio while financing the intricate creations for their next runway collection. Drawing from a captivating trove of archival footage alongside intimate observations of the trio at work, Sean Ono Lennon forges an affectionate portrait of uncompromising artists who have chosen experimentation over commercial success and a moving reflection on artistic collaboration and creative resilience. screenings.description: Just a Shot Away chronicles the brilliant and tumultuous life and career of Martin Scorsese, one of the world’s foremost living filmmakers, from his childhood on the violent streets of mid-century Little Italy, recreated in unprecedented detail, to his tectonic contributions to the cinema of the New Hollywood and beyond. screenings.title: Basic Instinct
screenings.description: The brainchild of provocateur extraordinaires Paul Verhoeven and Joe Eszterhas, Basic Instinct was one of the most controversial films of the 90s (protested by LGBTQ activists for its portrayal of the film’s bisexual femme fatale) and a runaway box office smash. When detective Nick Curran (Michael Douglas) becomes ensnared in a web of sex, lies, and violence, all the evidence points to Catherine Tramell (Sharon Stone, in a star-making role), a seductive, mysterious crime novelist. As the bodies pile up and hidden obsessions are revealed, Curran begins to doubt his investigatory instincts and give in to his baser ones.

screenings.title: The Crow Double Feature
screenings.description: A raw and self-reflective coming-of-age documentary, Inertia: Re-making The Crow follows two small-town teenagers in the 90’s as they obsessively recreate James O’Barr’s graphic novel. What starts as a simple after-school fan project becomes a four-year odyssey that consumes their entire high-school existence, and accidentally portrays the birth of two artists. Through intimate behind-the-scenes footage and candid interviews, the film reveals the passion, persistence, and resourcefulness of youthful creativity. (61min)

screenings.title: Rate It X
screenings.description: First released in 1985, RATE IT X stunned audiences and critics alike with its unflinching look at how sexism and sexual exploitation are embedded in American media and culture. Directors Lucy Winer and Paula de Koenigsberg traveled across the United States interviewing men who profited from—and helped perpetuate—stereotyped and sexualized images of women. Advertising executives describe how sex is used to sell product. Hustler magazine’s creator of the notorious “Chester the Molester” cartoon proudly displays drawings depicting a predatory adult man entrapping young girls. A fundamentalist minister tells us that Adam shirked his responsibility by allowing Eve to lead. The flamboyant producer of a popular cable show roams the streets of New York City in a silver lamé jumpsuit, video camera in hand, asking young women, “Would you like to flex into a hallway and pose nude?”

screenings.description: Few filmmakers have shown themselves so adept at plumbing the depths of the subconscious without coming up for air as Lynch, whose Lost Highway—inspired loosely by still-fresh coverage of the O. J. Simpson trial—begins as a dark domestic drama concerning a sexually incompetent saxophonist (Bill Pullman) and his wife (Patricia Arquette), morphs into a movie about a cocksman mechanic (Balthazar Getty) who gets involved with a gangster’s girl (Arquette, again), and ends with an unleashing of apocalyptic, purgative flame… Whether you take it as a cinematic depiction of a psychogenic fugue state or a free-associative disgorging of images from Hollywood’s id, Lynch’s film has the pull of a whirlpool and the terrible logic of a nightmare.

screenings.title: Cría Cuervos
screenings.description: Taking its title from the Spanish proverb “Raise ravens and they will pick your eyes out,” Saura’s lauded allegorical masterwork, set during the twilight of Spain’s Franco dictatorship, stars Ana Torrent (also seen in Spirit of the Beehive, in the same series) as a traumatized eight-year-old, second of three sisters living with a domineering aunt in Madrid following the death of their parents, who feels herself to be drifting freely between the worlds of the living and the dead and is increasingly convinced she has the ability to snuff out her adult persecutors’ lives. “Both an uncanny drama of family dysfunction and a historical parable of the end of Franco-ism… [Geraldine] Chaplin and Torrent are both outstanding.” —The Guardian

As loyalties blur and tensions erupt, survival depends on who can outthink — and outgun — everyone else.

screenings.title: Wings of Desire
screenings.description: In Wim Wenders’ iconic Wings of Desire, two angels, Damiel and Cassiel, glide through the streets of a divided Berlin, observing the bustling population. When Damiel falls in love with lonely trapeze artist Marion, the angel longs to experience life in the physical world. Featuring a showstopping performance by a young Nick Cave, crooning the title track from From Her to Eternity, Wings of Desire is one of the most inexhaustible modern films.

screenings.title: Cold Journey
screenings.description: Loosely based on the true story of Anishinaabe boy Charlie Wenjack, Cold Journey is a heart-wrenching tale of the profound pain wrought by forced assimilation, pinpointing the evils of residential schools decades before their injustices became mainstream knowledge. The only fictional feature by director Martin Defalco, the film captures its Indigenous communities in granular detail and through breathtaking images of the Canadian landscape. Featuring a stunning original song soundtrack by Indigenous musician and filmmaker Willie Dunn and a supporting turn from Chief Dan George (The Outlaw Josey Wales, Little Big Man), this is a long-overlooked but essential work of Indigenous Canadian cinema.

screenings.title: Raise the Red Lantern
screenings.description: China/Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Zhang Yimou Starring Gong Li, Saifei He, Jingwu Ma, Cuifen Cao In Mandarin with English subtitles Approx. 125 min. Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films and The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.title: Rome, Open City
screenings.description: “A STILL-THRILLING CALL TO CONSCIENCE AND HOPE! Shot with electrifying urgency months after Rome’s liberation… a cinematic landmark [that brought] Italian neorealism to world-wide attention. Born of wartime trauma and a desire for unity in the new Italy that would come, ROME, OPEN CITY has lost little of its power.” – Kristin M. Jones, Wall Street Journal Read the full review. “THE MOST PRECIOUS MOMENT OF FILM HISTORY!” – Martin Scorsese “ROSSELLINI’S NEOREALIST MASTERPIECE... Aldo Fabrizi is compelling as a sympathetic priest, as is Marcello Pagliero as a cool Communist. But towering over all is Anna Magnani, as a pregnant widow, mother and bride-to-be... Plain-spoken, tender and yet indomitable, she provides the film’s central anima.” – Andy Webster, New York Times “Rossellini’s tense, bloody, death-haunted film conjures an authenticity that’s based less on its quasi-documentary style than on a vision that brings ideas to life. It offers a template for a postwar renewal of Italy, as well as Italian cinema.” – Richard Brody, New Yorker “A LEGENDARY CINEMATIC ACHIEVEMENT! Its justly celebrated documentary aesthetic and naturalistic performances, aided by the filmmakers’ budgetary restrictions and the ruinous state of the postwar Italian film industry, help the work achieve moments of devastating, near miraculous beauty.” – Oleg Ivanov, Slant Read the full review. “The fame of Rossellini’s brutal, melodramatic account of the underground resistance to the Nazi occupation rest on its extraordinary immediacy and its rough, documentary look; at its most startling, it seems ‘caught’ rather than staged. screenings.description: From two⁠-⁠time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close⁠-⁠knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice. In Norwegian, English, Romanian and Swedish with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Asako I & II
screenings.description: Following up Happy Hour, his justly acclaimed epic of everyday life, Hamaguchi offers a different but no less quietly revolutionary vision with this pop romance that moves from youthful exuberance and delusion to mature circumspection and compromise, while keeping up throughout a magical tonal balance of wistfulness, comic buoyancy, and the ineffably heartbreaking. As a student in Osaka, Asako meets and falls in love with a drifter named Baku who one day drifts right out of her life. Two years later, working in Tokyo, she sees Baku again—or, rather, a young, solid businessman named Ryohei who is Baku’s double in every respect save personality. After initial astonishment, they begin to build a life together—but a twist in circumstances threatens to tear it all down, and forces Asako to confront her long, lingering love affair with a half-ghost fantasy.

screenings.title: The Woman in the Window
screenings.description: Alone for the holiday while his wife and children are on vacation, the staid, middle-aged college professor Richard Wanley (Edward G. Robinson) is about to settle in to an uneventful stretch of nights spent sipping port by the fireplace of his club—but then he catches a glimpse of a beguiling brunette in a gallery window and, in short order, finds himself having a drink with the model (Joan Bennett), after which everything goes straight to hell. Involved in a self-defense killing and its subsequent cover-up, Wanley finds himself investigating his own crime at the elbow of fellow clubman and D.A. Frank Lalor (Raymond Massey), the noose tightening around his neck with the emergence of every fresh clue and misstep. A high-style turning-of-the-screws noir suspenser, with a wonderfully oleaginous turn from heel extraordinaire Dan Duryea.

Drawing from a captivating trove of archival footage alongside intimate observations of the trio at work, Sean Ono Lennon forges an affectionate portrait of uncompromising artists who have chosen experimentation over commercial success and a moving reflection on artistic collaboration and creative resilience. screenings.title: Paisan
screenings.description: PAISÀ Italy, 1946 Directed by Roberto Rossellini Starring Carmela Sazio, Robert Van Loon, Dots Johnson Approx. 126 min. 35mm. The story of Italy’s liberation, told in six episodes, traveling from the first Allied landing in Sicily to the battle of the Po Delta, PAISAN demonstrated that OPEN CITY had been no fluke. Conceived on a vaster scale, with a considerably higher budget, and international distribution from MGM, PAISAN is a national epic that still startles for its immediacy, its technical mastery, its unpredictable rhythms. Scenes of unbearable suspense on the streets of Florence alternate with lighter fare, such as the doctrinal scuffles between Italian monks and American chaplains in Romagna. Stitched together like a newsreel (and skillfully edited to blend in stock footage and suggest off-screen pyrotechnics with creative sound effects), PAISAN became a worldwide sensation, an intellectual action film that pictured recent history with an unprecedented heft and scope. The film became a lodestar for filmmakers from Gillo Pontecorvo to Martin Scorsese, with the latter remarking, “The result... is still startling: it’s like seeing reality itself unfolding before your eyes.” 35mm print courtesy Cinecittà.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
screenings.description: “One of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I've ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker CRITIC’S PICK. “A house party for the ages... A blissout and one of the events of this cinematic season... A deeply personal, collectively produced oral history of a specific moment of time as it was lived—and held in memory—by specific individuals. The past comes vibrantly alive in these rooms, but always circles back to the present and often points to the future... One of the sustaining pleasures of this wonderful, spirit-lifting movie is that—even with many of its contributors now gone—it feels excitingly alive.” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “A MASTERPIECE... A truly monumental work of art.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine “The stuff of legend... Feels like a miracle.” – Robert Daniels, RogerEbert.com “An atmospheric, electrifying documentary, and a moving testament to the importance of remembering.” – Shirley Li, The Atlantic “An intergenerational feat... A documentary brimming with the wise, the thought-provoking and the deeply entertaining... [A] glimmering gift... with something that resembles a calling forth of the ancestors... A vivid and layered time capsule... Turns viewers into time travelers but also invited guests, rightly grateful to be in the room. For some of us, this film might evoke the wonder of a great-grandchild listening in on grown-up reminiscences. Nodding at the substance. Smiling at the style.” – Lisa Kennedy, Variety “[A] rich doc crafted from gorgeously restored footage. A triumph of DIY filmmaking and an act of cinematic resistance.” – Jourdain Searles, The Hollywood Reporter “A masterpiece.” – David Fear, Rolling Stone “Not only the biggest surprise of this year’s Sundance, but a revelation.” – Chris O’Falt, IndieWire

screenings.title: The Woman on the Beach
screenings.description: Though mutilated by RKO Pictures following a disastrous test screening, Renoir’s final Hollywood feature remains a film unlike any in its director’s filmography—not to speak of contemporary American cinema—a marvel of brooding atmosphere in which a Coast Guard officer haunted by the memory of a maritime tragedy (Robert Ryan), recently engaged, is bewitched by a dark beauty (Joan Bennett), the wife of a blind painter, whom he meets while riding at seaside, his attraction to her by no means unrequited. A disarmingly frank depiction of consuming, destructive erotic obsession, with a roiling, elemental score by Hanns Eisler contributing to the palpable sense of gathering doom.

screenings.title: That Day, On The Beach
screenings.description: The little-screened debut feature by Yang, prophet of and proselytizer for the Taiwanese New Wave, features Sylvia Chang and Terry Hu as two female friends, an unhappily married housewife and a concert pianist, brought together after a 13-year separation: their process of catching up illustrated through an innovative, ingeniously layered flashback structure which shows the director’s air for formal experimentation already fully in operation. Shot by renegade cinematographer Christopher Doyle, also on his first feature, Yang’s gorgeous and deeply felt memory piece/mystery uses its intricate structure to explore, among other things, “the ways in which patriarchal authority stunts young people’s lives.” US theatrical premiere of new 2K restoration.

screenings.title: Rome, Open City
screenings.description: “A STILL-THRILLING CALL TO CONSCIENCE AND HOPE! Shot with electrifying urgency months after Rome’s liberation… a cinematic landmark [that brought] Italian neorealism to world-wide attention. Born of wartime trauma and a desire for unity in the new Italy that would come, ROME, OPEN CITY has lost little of its power.” – Kristin M. Jones, Wall Street Journal Read the full review. “THE MOST PRECIOUS MOMENT OF FILM HISTORY!” – Martin Scorsese “ROSSELLINI’S NEOREALIST MASTERPIECE... Aldo Fabrizi is compelling as a sympathetic priest, as is Marcello Pagliero as a cool Communist. But towering over all is Anna Magnani, as a pregnant widow, mother and bride-to-be... Plain-spoken, tender and yet indomitable, she provides the film’s central anima.” – Andy Webster, New York Times “Rossellini’s tense, bloody, death-haunted film conjures an authenticity that’s based less on its quasi-documentary style than on a vision that brings ideas to life. It offers a template for a postwar renewal of Italy, as well as Italian cinema.” – Richard Brody, New Yorker “A LEGENDARY CINEMATIC ACHIEVEMENT! Its justly celebrated documentary aesthetic and naturalistic performances, aided by the filmmakers’ budgetary restrictions and the ruinous state of the postwar Italian film industry, help the work achieve moments of devastating, near miraculous beauty.” – Oleg Ivanov, Slant Read the full review. “The fame of Rossellini’s brutal, melodramatic account of the underground resistance to the Nazi occupation rest on its extraordinary immediacy and its rough, documentary look; at its most startling, it seems ‘caught’ rather than staged. screenings.title: Basic Instinct
screenings.description: The brainchild of provocateur extraordinaires Paul Verhoeven and Joe Eszterhas, Basic Instinct was one of the most controversial films of the 90s (protested by LGBTQ activists for its portrayal of the film’s bisexual femme fatale) and a runaway box office smash. When detective Nick Curran (Michael Douglas) becomes ensnared in a web of sex, lies, and violence, all the evidence points to Catherine Tramell (Sharon Stone, in a star-making role), a seductive, mysterious crime novelist. As the bodies pile up and hidden obsessions are revealed, Curran begins to doubt his investigatory instincts and give in to his baser ones.

screenings.title: Johnny O'clock
screenings.description: While gambling houses have existed as long as societies have, the nefarious business model of the modern casino has infiltrated every facet of the American economy. No current sporting event can be broadcast without some adjacent ads for the ever-growing list of online sportsbooks; celebrities shill browser-based casinos like Stake, and while the Big Apple hasn’t succumbed its real estate to Big Gambling (yet), we here at Spectacle are encouraging irresponsible financial behavior with three noir stories focused on one of humanity’s oldest vices.

screenings.title: Rate It X
screenings.description: First released in 1985, RATE IT X stunned audiences and critics alike with its unflinching look at how sexism and sexual exploitation are embedded in American media and culture. Directors Lucy Winer and Paula de Koenigsberg traveled across the United States interviewing men who profited from—and helped perpetuate—stereotyped and sexualized images of women. Advertising executives describe how sex is used to sell product. Hustler magazine’s creator of the notorious “Chester the Molester” cartoon proudly displays drawings depicting a predatory adult man entrapping young girls. A fundamentalist minister tells us that Adam shirked his responsibility by allowing Eve to lead. The flamboyant producer of a popular cable show roams the streets of New York City in a silver lamé jumpsuit, video camera in hand, asking young women, “Would you like to flex into a hallway and pose nude?”

screenings.title: Come Back to the 5 & Dime, Jimmy Dean, Jimmy Dean
screenings.description: One day in 1975, at a dusty Woolworth’s in small town McCarthy, Texas, the six members of the “Disciples of James Dean” reconvene 20 years after they first formed the club in the wake of the heartthrob actor’s death. Shifting between “present day” scenes and flashbacks to 1955 through an ingenious two-way mirror device, Altman’s film of Ed Graczyk’s play, which Altman had originally directed on the stage, is a touching meditation on dreams deferred and long-enduring female friendships, its peerless ensemble cast including Cher, Sandy Dennis, and Karen Black. Theatrical premiere of a new 4K restoration.

screenings.title: Fatherland
screenings.description: ★★★★★ “Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master.” – Phil de Semlyen, Time Out “A perfectly cut jewel of a movie... The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... Told with exacting restraint yet as layered as the lacquer on an ebony Biedermeier console, this forms a loose triptych with Pawlikowski’s last two features, IDA and COLD WAR, both of which were set at least partly behind the Iron Curtain... It is immaculately performed by Zischler and especially Hüller, grounding the film throughout with an uncanny, expressive stillness. But it is also exquisitely rendered in the same boxy ratio and silvery monochrome lensing Pawlikowski and DP Lukasz Zal (THE ZONE OF INTEREST) deployed on IDA and COLD WAR, and scrupulously detailed down to the ruined buildings, sharply cut suits, surly restaurant service and eclectic selection of jazz, classical and folk tunes chosen by Pawlikowski, all of which is sure to set discriminating viewers swooning.” – Leslie Felperin, The Hollywood Reporter

screenings.title: Drive
screenings.description: Drawing inspiration from Walter Hill’s The Driver, Refn’s high-style tour-de-force stars Ryan Gosling as a loner Los Angeles stunt driver who moonlights as a getaway wheelman on armed stickups, who’s put on a collision course with a nefarious criminal syndicate thanks to his protective affection for neighbor Carey Mulligan. A terse, tough, and morosely moody film propelled by a shimmering synth-pop score, with an extraordinary supporting cast that includes an against-type Albert Brooks as a sullen, profane gangster kingpin.

screenings.title: Best Pancakes in the County
screenings.description: Set over the course of one explosive night, BEST PANCAKES IN THE COUNTY transforms an unassuming small-town diner into the epicenter of a deadly standoff involving rogue federal agents, a fast-talking con man with a dangerous past and a waitress harboring secrets of her own. As loyalties blur and tensions erupt, survival depends on who can outthink — and outgun — everyone else.

screenings.title: Chinese Roulette
screenings.description: Fassbinder gives us the weekend getaway from hell in this suffocating chamber drama, in which unhappily and unfaithfully married couple Gerhard and Ariane Christ (Alexander Allerson and Margit Carstensen), intending to escape one another and their bitter disabled daughter, Angela (Andrea Schober), wind up in a family reunion, with lovers Anna Karina and Ulli Lommel in tow, at their country manse, where a vengeful Angela maneuvers the assembled parties into a round of the eponymous guessing game, designed to sow dissension and inflict maximum psychological torment. “More original and daring than anything I’ve yet to see by filmmakers who call themselves avant-garde… A mysterious comedy of deliberate elegance… Camp lyricism of such density it becomes a lethal weapon.” —The New York Times

screenings.title: 5 Against the House
screenings.description: While gambling houses have existed as long as societies have, the nefarious business model of the modern casino has infiltrated every facet of the American economy. No current sporting event can be broadcast without some adjacent ads for the ever-growing list of online sportsbooks; celebrities shill browser-based casinos like Stake, and while the Big Apple hasn’t succumbed its real estate to Big Gambling (yet), we here at Spectacle are encouraging irresponsible financial behavior with three noir stories focused on one of humanity’s oldest vices.

screenings.title: The History of Concrete
screenings.description: Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Raise the Red Lantern
screenings.description: China/Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Zhang Yimou Starring Gong Li, Saifei He, Jingwu Ma, Cuifen Cao In Mandarin with English subtitles Approx. 125 min. Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films and The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.title: All of a Sudden
screenings.description: Japan’s Official Selection for Best International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards® WINNER, BEST ACTRESS (VIRGINIE EFIRA & TAO OKAMOTO), 2026 CANNES FILM FESTIVAL In the latest film by Oscar®-winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi (DRIVE MY CAR), Virginie Efira (BENEDETTA) stars as Marie-Lou, the progressive director of a nursing home in the Parisian suburbs. Her life changes when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), Japanese playwright. As the two women reckon with the lives they have lived, they find new ways to make sense of the time that remains. Following caregivers as they navigate the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a film that rests fully in the present, attentive to the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and human connection. Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films 2026 196 MIN. screenings.title: Fatherland
screenings.description: ★★★★★ “Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master.” – Phil de Semlyen, Time Out “A perfectly cut jewel of a movie... The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... Told with exacting restraint yet as layered as the lacquer on an ebony Biedermeier console, this forms a loose triptych with Pawlikowski’s last two features, IDA and COLD WAR, both of which were set at least partly behind the Iron Curtain... It is immaculately performed by Zischler and especially Hüller, grounding the film throughout with an uncanny, expressive stillness. But it is also exquisitely rendered in the same boxy ratio and silvery monochrome lensing Pawlikowski and DP Lukasz Zal (THE ZONE OF INTEREST) deployed on IDA and COLD WAR, and scrupulously detailed down to the ruined buildings, sharply cut suits, surly restaurant service and eclectic selection of jazz, classical and folk tunes chosen by Pawlikowski, all of which is sure to set discriminating viewers swooning.” – Leslie Felperin, The Hollywood Reporter

screenings.title: L'amore
screenings.description: Italy, 1948 Directed by Roberto Rossellini Starring Anna Magnani, Federico Fellini, Peparuolo, Amelia Robert In Italian with English subtitles. Approx. 80 min. 35mm. Conceived as an homage to the range and artistry of Anna Magnani, L’AMORE is a diptych that drags the actress to the brink and watches, mouth agape, as she leaps into the abyss. The first part—“The Human Voice”—adapts a one-act play by Jean Cocteau, which Magnani had performed on stage in 1942, playing a woman whose only connection to her lover runs through the telephone wire. Shot in a French studio over two weeks with money that Rossellini had procured for GERMANY YEAR ZERO, this intensely claustrophobic showcase for Magnani (and her dog, Micia) renders a break-up as a world-historic event—as it always is for those so spurned. The second episode—“The Miracle”—was based on an original idea by Fellini, who also co-stars as a silent vagabond whom Magnani’s talkative goatherd believes to be the incarnation of Saint Joseph. Throwing herself upon the saint’s blissful body, Magnani wakes in a daze, pregnant and ever closer to the divine. If the monks can report sightings of the Madonna, why cannot Magnani follow her holy path? Although “The Miracle” aroused no complaints from the Vatican, it faced extraordinary hostility in the US, where the lay Catholics of the Legion of Decency launched a successful campaign for the New York Board of Regents to rescind the film’s exhibition license on the basis of alleged sacrilege. Distributor Joseph Burstyn appealed the decision all the way to the Supreme Court, which ultimately ruled in his favor, belatedly bringing cinema under the protection of the First Amendment, and sowing the seeds of censorship’s demise. A miracle indeed. 35mm print courtesy Cinecittà. Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film

screenings.title: The Host
screenings.description: When a terrifying creature rises from the Han River and brings chaos to Seoul, single dad Gang-du (Song Kang-ho, Parasite) will stop at nothing to rescue his daughter from the clutches of the horrifying Host. Equal parts creature-feature thrill ride and poignant human story, Oscar-winning visionary Bong Joon Ho’s first global smash remains an incredible action drama and propulsively entertaining modern classic.

Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice. In Norwegian, English, Romanian and Swedish with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Rate It X
screenings.description: First released in 1985, RATE IT X stunned audiences and critics alike with its unflinching look at how sexism and sexual exploitation are embedded in American media and culture. Directors Lucy Winer and Paula de Koenigsberg traveled across the United States interviewing men who profited from—and helped perpetuate—stereotyped and sexualized images of women. Advertising executives describe how sex is used to sell product. Hustler magazine’s creator of the notorious “Chester the Molester” cartoon proudly displays drawings depicting a predatory adult man entrapping young girls. A fundamentalist minister tells us that Adam shirked his responsibility by allowing Eve to lead. The flamboyant producer of a popular cable show roams the streets of New York City in a silver lamé jumpsuit, video camera in hand, asking young women, “Would you like to flex into a hallway and pose nude?”

screenings.title: Threeasfour: Full Circle
screenings.description: Avant-garde designers and best friends Gabi Asfour, Angela Donhauser, and Adi Gil have spent 25 years working together as the NYC fashion collective threeASFOUR. Although they have built an impressive reputation and a following that includes Björk, Marisa Tomei, and Chloë Sevigny, they find themselves struggling to pay the rent on their Chinatown studio while financing the intricate creations for their next runway collection. Drawing from a captivating trove of archival footage alongside intimate observations of the trio at work, Sean Ono Lennon forges an affectionate portrait of uncompromising artists who have chosen experimentation over commercial success and a moving reflection on artistic collaboration and creative resilience. Presented with support from The Endowed Fund for Emerging Filmmakers and The Roy Lichtenstein Foundation Fund 2026 95 MIN. USA IN ENGLISH, GERMAN, AND ARABIC WITH ENGLISH SUBTITLES ASSEMBLY RELEASING

screenings.title: Rome, Open City
screenings.description: “A STILL-THRILLING CALL TO CONSCIENCE AND HOPE! Shot with electrifying urgency months after Rome’s liberation… a cinematic landmark [that brought] Italian neorealism to world-wide attention. Born of wartime trauma and a desire for unity in the new Italy that would come, ROME, OPEN CITY has lost little of its power.” – Kristin M. Jones, Wall Street Journal Read the full review. “THE MOST PRECIOUS MOMENT OF FILM HISTORY!” – Martin Scorsese “ROSSELLINI’S NEOREALIST MASTERPIECE... Aldo Fabrizi is compelling as a sympathetic priest, as is Marcello Pagliero as a cool Communist. But towering over all is Anna Magnani, as a pregnant widow, mother and bride-to-be... Plain-spoken, tender and yet indomitable, she provides the film’s central anima.” – Andy Webster, New York Times “Rossellini’s tense, bloody, death-haunted film conjures an authenticity that’s based less on its quasi-documentary style than on a vision that brings ideas to life. It offers a template for a postwar renewal of Italy, as well as Italian cinema.” – Richard Brody, New Yorker “A LEGENDARY CINEMATIC ACHIEVEMENT! Its justly celebrated documentary aesthetic and naturalistic performances, aided by the filmmakers’ budgetary restrictions and the ruinous state of the postwar Italian film industry, help the work achieve moments of devastating, near miraculous beauty.” – Oleg Ivanov, Slant Read the full review. “The fame of Rossellini’s brutal, melodramatic account of the underground resistance to the Nazi occupation rest on its extraordinary immediacy and its rough, documentary look; at its most startling, it seems ‘caught’ rather than staged. Many Americans, used to slick war films, reacted to it as if it actually were caught… The movie gave us a cross-section of a city under terrible stress.” – Pauline Kael “Rossellini’s Neo-Realism masterpiece... It scarcely matters how many times you watch it... The story plays like a gripping thriller: a cat-and-mouse game between Gestapo and resistance cell.” – Cath Clarke, The Guardian “Still a picture of unrivaled immediacy and passion... memorably preserved a place and a time—and taught generations of filmmakers how to preserve theirs.” – Michael Wilmington “ALL ROADS LEAD TO ROME, OPEN CITY.” – Godard

screenings.description: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter island by their bureau chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi). Amongst the Island’s iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris’s newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.

screenings.title: Suzhou River
screenings.description: Taking its name from the polluted river that flows through Shanghai, director Lou’s hometown, the brooding Suzhou River uses the singular first-person perspective of its unseen videographer-narrator to explore the grubby underbelly of the city, observing the story of an unsuspecting motorcycle courier who finds himself snared in a kidnapping plot and murder rap. A seductive, intricately structured stylistic coup from the Sixth Generation filmmaker, drawing on influences from film noir to Vertigo (1958) while developing its own idiosyncratic and haunting visual vocabulary.

screenings.title: News from Home + Interior NY Subway, 14th Street
screenings.description: Akerman was 26 years old and living in New York City, away from her native Belgium and her mother, when she teamed with DP Babette Mangolte to film this diary/essay/poem in subway stations and on street corners, their images to eventually be paired with Akerman’s recitals of her mother’s fretful letters. Arguably this extraordinary filmmaker’s most perfect and poignant nonfiction work, both one of the greatest portraits of a city ever put on film and a troubling, touching depiction of maternal love. Screens in the English-language version.

screenings.title: Paisan
screenings.description: PAISÀ Italy, 1946 Directed by Roberto Rossellini Starring Carmela Sazio, Robert Van Loon, Dots Johnson Approx. 126 min. 35mm. The story of Italy’s liberation, told in six episodes, traveling from the first Allied landing in Sicily to the battle of the Po Delta, PAISAN demonstrated that OPEN CITY had been no fluke. Conceived on a vaster scale, with a considerably higher budget, and international distribution from MGM, PAISAN is a national epic that still startles for its immediacy, its technical mastery, its unpredictable rhythms. Scenes of unbearable suspense on the streets of Florence alternate with lighter fare, such as the doctrinal scuffles between Italian monks and American chaplains in Romagna. Stitched together like a newsreel (and skillfully edited to blend in stock footage and suggest off-screen pyrotechnics with creative sound effects), PAISAN became a worldwide sensation, an intellectual action film that pictured recent history with an unprecedented heft and scope. The film became a lodestar for filmmakers from Gillo Pontecorvo to Martin Scorsese, with the latter remarking, “The result... is still startling: it’s like seeing reality itself unfolding before your eyes.” 35mm print courtesy Cinecittà.

screenings.description: A “quiet mixture of science fiction with a love story as subtle as anything in Rohmer or Rivette” [Raymond Durgnat], Resnais’s definition-defying film stars Claude Rich as an unsuccessful suicide who, on leaving hospital, agrees to participate in an experiment in time travel—one that will bring fragments of his past rushing back is disordered shards.

screenings.title: Autumn Sonata
screenings.description: Ingmar and Ingrid, Bergman and Bergman, together at last. Sweden’s most popular export before the Volvo, in her final screen role, plays a world-renowned concert pianist who returns home to reunite with her now-married daughter (Liv Ullmann), long a distant second to her mother’s career ambitions, the two women exhuming old resentments and struggling towards reconciliation over the course of an emotionally draining 24 hours. “So unrelenting, so harrowing, that I walked out of the theater on shaking legs. If you’re open to the experience that Bergman means to provide, you may leave the film muttering a wrung-out ‘Whew!’ followed quickly by an appreciative ‘Wow!’” —Richard Corliss, Time Magazine

Directors Lucy Winer and Paula de Koenigsberg traveled across the United States interviewing men who profited from—and helped perpetuate—stereotyped and sexualized images of women. Advertising executives describe how sex is used to sell product. Hustler magazine’s creator of the notorious “Chester the Molester” cartoon proudly displays drawings depicting a predatory adult man entrapping young girls. A fundamentalist minister tells us that Adam shirked his responsibility by allowing Eve to lead. The flamboyant producer of a popular cable show roams the streets of New York City in a silver lamé jumpsuit, video camera in hand, asking young women, “Would you like to flex into a hallway and pose nude?”

screenings.title: Come Back to the 5 & Dime, Jimmy Dean, Jimmy Dean
screenings.description: One day in 1975, at a dusty Woolworth’s in small town McCarthy, Texas, the six members of the “Disciples of James Dean” reconvene 20 years after they first formed the club in the wake of the heartthrob actor’s death. Shifting between “present day” scenes and flashbacks to 1955 through an ingenious two-way mirror device, Altman’s film of Ed Graczyk’s play, which Altman had originally directed on the stage, is a touching meditation on dreams deferred and long-enduring female friendships, its peerless ensemble cast including Cher, Sandy Dennis, and Karen Black.
